title: Establishing a call from its body
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let $p,d,T$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{args}$ be a finite list of integers, let $\mu : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{Z}$ be an initial memory, and let $Q$ be a predicate on an integer and a memory function. Suppose procedure $p$ in $P$ has body $s$, and executing $s$ from the state whose locations are initialized by $\mathrm{args}$ and whose memory is $\mu$ can finish within cost $T$ with output and final memory satisfying $Q$. Then the call to procedure $p$ on $\mathrm{args}$ from memory $\mu$ at depth $d$ meets cost bound $T$ and postcondition $Q$.
hypotheses_covered: A finite list of integer arguments $\mathrm{args}$
A postcondition $Q$ on output and memory
Executing $s$ from the argument-initialized state and memory $\mu$ meets cost bound $T$ and $Q$
